title: How does a new user get a memory profile?
lead: Should the new Account card get a Profile section that creates a private profile on first run and can turn an export from another assistant into a first draft for the user to approve? I recommend it: today a new user starts with no profile unless they find a template folder and copy it by hand.
for_you: Account card gains a Profile section: it shows whether a profile exists, with Create and Import buttons
On first run the hub shows one small prompt pointing there, with a Not now exit
Your own profile is untouched: it already exists, so you only see its status

for_you.text: An import is drafted by an agent and lands as one batch you approve, like core lessons today

context: Matt (2026-11-17): a new user who downloads Crux gets no memory setup. Today the public repo ships profile-template/ (blank core.md and packs/_index.md) and a README saying to copy it into ~/crux/profile/ and keep that folder private (decisions 14, 15). Nothing in the hub's setup mentions it. Matt's own profile was seeded from his Claude.ai memory export and older notes; a newcomer's grows only from lessons, and it is untested whether propose_lesson works with no profile folder at all. Matt wants this to live in the Account card from decision 78.

options.name: Create plus import, in the Account card
options.summary: A Profile section in the Account card. Create makes ~/crux/profile from the template (core, pack index, empty private file) and makes ~/crux a local private git repo with no remote. Import takes a pasted or dropped memory export from another assistant; an agent sorts it into core, packs and private, treating it as data, and the result waits as one batch for approval. First run shows one small prompt pointing there.
pros: A newcomer gets a useful profile on day one, as Matt did
Nothing joins the profile without the user's yes
cons: The import step costs one agent run and needs care with what the export contains

options.name: Create only
options.summary: As A without import: Create makes the blank profile, and lessons fill it over time.
pros: Smallest; no agent run, nothing pasted in
cons: Starts empty; agents know nothing about the user for weeks

options.name: A, plus a short first-run interview
options.summary: As A, and for users with no export: a five-minute chat with an agent (role, how they like work approved, tone, UI likes) that drafts the core for approval.
pros: Everyone starts with a real core, export or not
cons: Most to build; an interview can feel like homework

recommendation: A: Create and Import in the Account card's Profile section, everything approved as one batch. An interview (C) can follow if users without an export start too empty.
change_mind: If most new users have no export to import, add the interview (C).

settles.value: Profile section in the hub's Account card: create a blank private profile from the template on first run (home crux folder as a local private git repo), optional import of another assistant's memory export drafted by an agent and approved as one batch
